gates.reason: Checked CLI-derived paths, receipt and ledger reads/writes, symlink rejection, bounded file reads, secret exposure, command execution, and LLM egress; no exploitable defect was found.
A completed async Sidekick row without a corresponding queued row is accepted as settled and contributes to trigger, paid-call, and cost totals.
Accounting inputs have explicit byte and row limits, evidence is processed in bounded in-memory passes, and no release-blocking hotspot was verified.

findings.title: Orphan async completion rows are counted as valid accounting evidence
findings.what: The completed-row branch creates a new job with queued=false when no queued row exists, then marks it completed and adds its cost to paidRows. The lifecycle check at line 906 rejects only queued && !completed, so completed && !queued survives. It is consequently included in asyncJobs.size, paidRows.length, and the summed Sidekick cost, allowing unsupported ledger rows to produce eligible accounting claims.
findings.fix: Treat every async job as complete only when both queued and completed are true. Reject or demote completed-without-queued and queued-without-completed lifecycles before calculating any async trigger, paid-call, or cost totals.
findings.acceptance: Feed collectSidekickRows a valid-looking completed Sidekick row with a unique jobId but no matching queued row. The result must carry a lifecycle-incomplete/conflict unknown reason, expose null cost and paid-call totals, and be excluded from eligible all-in accounting. A matched queued-plus-completed pair must remain counted exactly once.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 849-860 synthesize and accept a missing queued state, while lines 905-909 test only queued-without-completed. No later validation requires completed jobs to have been queued before totals are emitted.
